The numbers 1, 2, ..., 2100 are written on a board. Every second, Mark takes two numbers on the board, \( a \) and \( b \), erases them, and replaces them with \( \gcd(a, b) \) and \( \operatorname{lcm}(a, b) \). Mark stops once any move he makes will not change the numbers written on the board. Compute the number of divisors of the 2026th smallest positive integer written on the board when he finishes.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

# Finding the 2026th Smallest Number After Convergence

## Key Invariant

Each move replaces $a, b$ with $\gcd(a,b), \operatorname{lcm}(a,b)$. For each prime $p$, if $a = p^x \cdot \cdots$ and $b = p^y \cdot \cdots$, the exponents change from $\{x, y\}$ to $\{\min(x,y), \max(x,y)\}$ — **the same multiset**.

**Therefore, for each prime $p$, the multiset of exponents $\{v_p(n) : n = 1, \ldots, 2100\}$ is invariant.**

## Identifying the Final State

Mark stops when no move changes the board, meaning every pair satisfies divisibility — the numbers form a **chain** $a_1 \mid a_2 \mid \cdots \mid a_{2100}$.

In a divisibility chain, each prime's exponents must be non-decreasing. Since the exponent multisets are invariant, the final state is **uniquely determined**:

$$a_k = \prod_p p^{e_p(k)}$$

where $e_p(k)$ is the $k$-th smallest value in $\{v_p(n) : n = 1, \ldots, 2100\}$.

The 2026th smallest number is $a_{2026}$.

## Computing $e_p(2026)$ for Each Prime

For each prime $p$, I count how many numbers have $v_p(n) = 0, 1, 2, \ldots$ and locate position 2026:

| Prime $p$ | $\lfloor 2100/p^k \rfloor$ values | Zeros | 1s | 2s | 3s | 4s | 5s | 6s+ | Cumulative at each level | $e_p(2026)$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 1050,525,262,131,65,32,16,8,4,2,1 | 1050 | 525 | 263 | 131 | 66 | 33 | ... | 1969 (≤3), 2035 (≤4) | **4** |
| 3 | 700,233,77,25,8,2 | 1400 | 467 | 156 | 52 | 17 | 6 | 2 | 2023 (≤2), 2075 (≤3) | **3** |
| 5 | 420,84,16,3 | 1680 | 336 | 68 | 13 | 3 | — | — | 2016 (≤1), 2084 (≤2) | **2** |
| 7 | 300,42,6 | 1800 | 258 | 36 | 6 | — | — | — | 1800, 2058 (≤1) | **1** |
| 11 | 190,17,1 | 1910 | 173 | 16 | 1 | — | — | — | 1910, 2083 (≤1) | **1** |
| 13 | 161,12 | 1939 | 149 | 12 | — | — | — | — | 1939, 2088 (≤1) | **1** |
| 17 | 123,7 | 1977 | 116 | 7 | — | — | — | — | 1977, 2093 (≤1) | **1** |
| 19 | 110,5 | 1990 | 105 | 5 | — | — | — | — | 1990, 2095 (≤1) | **1** |
| 23 | 91,3 | 2009 | 88 | 3 | — | — | — | — | 2009, 2097 (≤1) | **1** |
| 29+ | — | ≥2028 | — | — | — | — | — | — | 2028+ (≥2026) | **0** |

## The 2026th Number

$$a_{2026} = 2^4 \cdot 3^3 \cdot 5^2 \cdot 7^1 \cdot 11^1 \cdot 13^1 \cdot 17^1 \cdot 19^1 \cdot 23^1$$

## Counting Divisors

$$\tau(a_{2026}) = (4+1)(3+1)(2+1)(1+1)^6 = 5 \times 4 \times 3 \times 2^6 = 60 \times 64 = 3840$$

$$\boxed{3840}$$
